almanac: first day of month / turn of month -> C1c,C1i
week after triple witching, expiry -> C1b,C1f
first month of quarter, December low, best six months, MACD timing: <= 6 observations on crypto -> cannot be known (C1e)
hofm: losses come from over-betting plus lack of diversification in one scenario: the T1 ladder is exactly this (80 fills in one minute) -> E2d
'forced liquidation at unfavourable prices: gap moves through stops' -> same finding as T1j (stops hurt)
managers double up: never reload T1 in the same event
artemis: 97% of strategies are implicitly short volatility -> T1, flow, listing shorts and funding capture all are; tsmom is the only long-convexity book -> check combined tail (E2d), do not add T1 size on top of other short-vol books

not_transferable: Artemis and HOFM contain no trading rule; presidential cycle, sector tables, decennial cycle

new_forms.what: Almanac p120: a down Friday followed by a down Monday marks an inflection (lower over the next weeks), vs down Friday / up Monday and vs any two down days of equal size; BTC and equal-weight top-30

Almanac p175 tax-loss 'free lunch': coins within 5% of their 52-week low on Dec 15 -> until Feb 15 vs the rest (cross-section, clean bnall); placebo = the same on the 15th of every other month; only 5-6 Decembers, so report effect and MDE, verdict limited
Almanac p139, p226: FIRST day of the month (12x an average day) and last + first four days; split C1c into these two exact windows before looking at the table

T1 is short crash insurance (Artemis: 'short convexity'; HOFM: overbetting kills, not being wrong): daily P&L of the ladder vs tsmom / flow shadow returns in the 20 worst weeks, and size from a fractional-Kelly with a worst case of -50% on every simultaneous fill added by hand, vs the 5% rule
